newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mobil Singapore to delay refinery startup-sources.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Singapore to delay refinery startup-sources.

text.p: Mobil Oil Singapore, which has earlier scheduled to restart its refinery next week from routine maintenance, might be forced to delay it due to a series of mishaps during the shutdown, industry sources said on Thursday.
Mobil shut down its 280,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery and 500,000 tonne-per-year petrochemical complex on March 15 for maintence work and to upgrade the refinery's capacity to 300,000-bpd.
Before the turnaround, a company spokesman said the work was "expected to last for about a month".
A Mobil spokeswoman declined to comment on the exact date, but said it will be announced closer to the start-up.
But sources told Reuters the scheduled restart, slated for April 23-25, was expected to have "some set back" due to a number of accidents which plagued the maintenance.
The first was a flash fire on March 26 which was extinguished within five minutes and did not affect the maintenance work, a company spokeswoman had said.
On March 31, a gas leak at an aromatics plants led to the death of two men and five injuries. Maintenance work at the plant was suspended for two days.
On March 31, firefighters took 27 minutes to extinguish a fire in the morning, while in the afternoon some smouldering was put out at one of the tanks.
